title: Input to the `knowledge.get` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `knowledge.get`. SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2).

**Unknown keys are refused rather than dropped.** The SDK builds its argument model from the handler's annotations and sets no `extra="forbid"`, so a key it does not recognise is discarded before any Theurian code runs. On this tool that silence is the one that matters most: a caller who misspells `includeUnapproved` is told nothing, and reads the refusal that follows as "no such item" (ADR-0031 decision 4).

**Composition.** The context every project-scoped call carries — `projectId`, and the optional `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` — arrives by `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json` rather than being restated here. The closure is `unevaluatedProperties: false` and not `additionalProperties: false`, which under a `$ref` composition rejects the very context fields it referenced (ADR-0031 decision 1, measured against `jsonschema` 4.26.0). `projectId` is required by the referent and is not repeated in this file's `required`.

**Three referenced context fields are accepted and read by nothing.** `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` are the referent's, and no handler in this build takes them, so a call that sets one is answered as if it had not.

**What this file constrains, and what it leaves to the handler.** Shape and length. The identifier grammar stays a handler refusal: `ItemId` rejects a malformed id with a message that names `knowledge.search` as the way to find a real one, and a `pattern` here would answer "does not satisfy" in its place.

itemId.description:
Which item to fetch. An alias resolves to the item it names, so a renamed item stays reachable by the id a caller already holds.

At most 200 characters, which is `MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH` — the bound `ItemId` itself enforces, so no stored id can be longer and a longer one could name nothing. Bounded here as well because an over-long id is otherwise carried into an error message: the handler reports its length rather than quoting it, and this refuses it before either happens (#17).

A well-formed id this caller may not read and one that was never stored are the same answer, deliberately (SEC-13). Nothing about that distinction is expressible here, and nothing here narrows it.

includeUnapproved.description: Whether a draft or proposal may be returned. Defaults to `false`, and never reaches retired knowledge: a `rejected`, `deprecated` or `superseded` revision is withheld from every caller on every path, because closing that door in `knowledge.search` alone would achieve nothing — a caller reads an approved item, takes the `targetItemId` off its `rejects` relation, and fetches the withheld body in one more call (SEC-13).
